# google-docs-mcp — full reference

FastMCP 3.4.4+ server exposing Google Docs (content editing, Docs API v1) and Google Drive
(file lifecycle, Drive API v3) as MCP tools. Runs locally as a stdio process launched by
Claude Desktop; OAuth uses the installed-app (desktop) flow with a loopback redirect — no
data passes through any third-party server, only directly between the user's machine and
Google's own APIs.

## Why two APIs, one server

Google Docs API v1 only edits document *content* (paragraphs, text runs, tables, styles) via
one `documents.batchUpdate` endpoint taking typed request objects. Everything about a document
as a *file* — listing, searching, sharing, permissions, trash, revisions, comments — lives in
Drive API v3, because a Google Doc is a Drive file with a special mimeType
(`application/vnd.google-apps.document`). This server mirrors that split as two portmanteau
tools rather than merging them, so the tool surface matches Google's own API boundary.

## Tool surface

### google_docs_auth(operation)

OAuth lifecycle. Operations: `status` (read-only — configured/authenticated/scopes/token_path/
expiry), `start_oauth` (opens the user's browser, blocks until consent completes — MUST be
announced to the user before calling), `revoke` (deletes the cached token file).

### google_docs(operation, ...)

Docs API v1 content editing. Operations:

- `create(title)` → `{document_id, url}`
- `get(document_id)` → raw Docs API document JSON
- `read_text(document_id)` → plain-text body
- `get_structure(document_id)` → outline of headings/paragraphs with `{start_index, end_index,
  style, text}`
- `insert_text(document_id, text, index)` / `append_text(document_id, text)`
- `delete_range(document_id, start_index, end_index)`
- `replace_all_text(document_id, find_text, replace_text, match_case)`
- `insert_page_break(document_id, index)`
- `insert_table(document_id, rows, columns, index)`
- `update_paragraph_style(document_id, start_index, end_index, alignment, named_style_type)`
- `update_text_style(document_id, start_index, end_index, bold, italic, underline, font_size,
  foreground_color)`
- `batch_update(document_id, requests)` — raw Docs API request passthrough for anything not
  covered above (nested lists, footnotes, headers/footers, embedded images, suggested edits)

**Indices are UTF-16 code unit offsets and shift after every edit.** Always re-fetch
`get_structure` between edits in the same document rather than reusing a stale index.

### google_drive(operation, ...)

Drive API v3 file lifecycle. Operations:

- `list_files(folder_id?, docs_only=True, limit=25, cursor?)` — paginated
- `search(query, docs_only=True, limit=25, cursor?)` — full-text + metadata search, paginated
- `get_metadata(file_id)`
- `create_folder(name, folder_id?)`
- `copy(file_id, name?, folder_id?)` / `move(file_id, new_parent_id)` / `rename(file_id, name)`
- `trash(file_id)` (reversible) / `untrash(file_id)` / `delete_permanently(file_id,
  confirm=True)` (**irreversible, bypasses trash — requires explicit confirm=True**)
- `share(file_id, email, role="reader", send_notification=True)`
- `list_permissions(file_id)` / `revoke_permission(file_id, permission_id)`
- `list_revisions(file_id, limit=25, cursor?)` — paginated
- `list_comments(file_id, limit=25, cursor?)` — paginated
- `add_comment(file_id, content)` / `reply_comment(file_id, comment_id, content)` /
  `resolve_comment(file_id, comment_id)`
- `export(file_id, export_format="pdf", output_path)` — download a Doc as pdf/docx/odt/txt/html/rtf/epub
  (10 MB Drive API export limit)
- `import_file(file_path, name?, folder_id?)` — upload a local .docx/.odt/.txt/.md/.html/.rtf and
  convert it into a new Google Doc
- `browse(folder_id?, limit=25, cursor?)` — folders + Google Docs directly inside `folder_id`
  (Drive root if omitted), plus breadcrumbs back to root. Folders are unpaginated (bounded —
  200 max, realistic for any folder tree); the docs list is paginated the same way as
  `list_files`/`search`
- `backup_folder(output_dir, folder_id?, export_format="pdf", recursive=False)` — exports every
  doc in a folder to local files, writes a `manifest.json` (`{doc_id, name, local_path,
  modified_time}` per file)
- `restore_file(file_id, file_path)` — overwrites an **existing** Google Doc's content from a
  local file (the inverse of `export`/`import_file`, which always create new docs)

Pagination: paginated operations return `{items, has_more, next_cursor}` inside `data` — pass
`next_cursor` back as `cursor` to continue.

### google_docs_convert_advanced(file_id, output_format, output_path)

Bridges to a sibling **libreoffice-mcp** server via a real MCP client call (FastMCP `Client`,
not a subprocess) for output formats Drive's native `export` can't produce: `doc`, `fodt`,
`rtf` (plus `odt`, `txt`, `pdf`, `html`, which Drive can already do — routed through
LibreOffice anyway for a single consistent code path). Exports the doc to a temp docx via
`google_drive(operation="export")` first, then calls libreoffice-mcp's `libreoffice(operation=
"convert")`. If libreoffice-mcp isn't reachable at `LIBREOFFICE_MCP_URL` (default
`http://127.0.0.1:10981/mcp`), returns `error_type: "dependency_unavailable"` — distinct from
this server's own `not_configured`/`not_authenticated`.

### google_docs_sync(operation, ...)

Polling two-way sync between a local folder and a Drive folder — like OneDrive Desktop, but
checked on an interval rather than pushed instantly (no public HTTPS endpoint for Google's
`files.watch` push notifications is realistic for a local desktop app). Operations:

- `configure(local_dir, folder_id?, interval_seconds=300, export_format="docx")` — sets up (or
  replaces) the pair; does not itself start background polling
- `status()` — current config, whether background polling is active, tracked doc count
- `run_once()` — synchronous single reconcile pass, returns `{pulled, pushed, conflicts,
  remote_deleted, untracked_missing_local, errors, ran_at}`
- `enable()` / `disable()` — toggle background polling at `interval_seconds` (min 60); config
  and manifest are kept across `disable`, not deleted

Safety defaults: a doc changed on **both** sides since the last sync is a conflict (local edit
renamed with a timestamp suffix and kept, Drive's version becomes canonical — never silently
overwritten); a doc trashed on Drive moves the local file to a `_remote_deleted/` subfolder
(never hard-deleted); a file deleted locally self-heals by being re-pulled next pass (Drive is
authoritative, a local `rm` never cascades into deleting the Drive doc). The Starlette backend
runs this on a background `asyncio` task alongside its own lifespan, polling every
`interval_seconds` while `enabled`; a failed pass is logged and never kills the loop.

### google_docs_mcp_help()

Static markdown tool reference, no network calls, no parameters.

### show_google_docs_status_app()

Prefab UI (`@mcp.tool(app=True)`) status card — same data as `google_docs_auth(status)`,
rendered as a rich in-chat card with a plain-text fallback for hosts without MCP Apps support.

### show_google_drive_folder_app(folder_id?)

Prefab UI card — same data as `google_drive(operation="browse", folder_id=...)`, rendered as
tables (folders, docs) with breadcrumbs instead of a dict.

### show_google_docs_sync_status_app()

Prefab UI card — same data as `google_docs_sync(operation="status")`, rendered as a status
card (local folder, Drive folder, poll interval, tracked-doc count, enabled/disabled badge).

## Tool annotation hints

Every tool sets FastMCP `annotations=` (`readOnlyHint`/`destructiveHint`/`idempotentHint`/
`openWorldHint`) on its registration in `server.py`. Portmanteau tools mixing read/write/
destructive operations use the worst-case hint — `google_drive` sets `destructiveHint=True`
because of `delete_permanently`, even though most of its operations aren't destructive.

## Return shape (every tool)

Success: `{"success": true, "message": str, "data": {...}}`
Failure: `{"success": false, "error": str, "error_type": str, "suggestions": [str]}`

`error_type` values and what they mean:

- `not_configured` — `GOOGLE_DOCS_MCP_CLIENT_ID`/`_SECRET` env vars unset. Fix: docs/ONBOARDING.md.
- `not_authenticated` — OAuth client configured but no valid cached token. Fix: call
  `google_docs_auth(operation="start_oauth")`.
- `validation` — missing/bad parameter for the chosen operation. Fix the call; do not retry blindly.
- `permission` — signed-in Google account lacks access to the file. Ask the owner to share it.
- `not_found` — bad `document_id`/`file_id`. Re-search via `google_drive(operation="search")`.
- `conflict` — Google API returned HTTP 409.
- `rate_limited` — Docs/Drive API quota hit. Wait a few seconds, retry once.
- `api_error` — any other Google API error, message carries detail.
- `dependency_unavailable` — `google_docs_convert_advanced` only: libreoffice-mcp isn't
  reachable at `LIBREOFFICE_MCP_URL`. Distinct from `not_configured`/`not_authenticated`,
  which are about this server's own Google OAuth setup, not the other server's availability.

## Architecture

No local database — Google Docs/Drive are the sole source of truth; the only local state is
the cached OAuth token at `data/token.json` (gitignored, plaintext, same trust model as
`claude_desktop_config.json`). This server therefore skips the fleet's HTTP-daemon +
stdio-proxy pattern (SOTA_REQUIREMENTS.md §2.3) — that pattern exists to prevent concurrent
stdio clients from corrupting a local SQLite/LanceDB file, and there is no such file here.

Dual transport: `google_docs_mcp.server:mcp` runs over stdio (the `google-docs-mcp` console
script, what Claude Desktop launches) and is also exposed as an ASGI sub-app (`mcp_http_app`)
mounted at `/mcp` on the Starlette webapp backend (port 11972; frontend 11973), so the
webapp's own Chat page can reach the same tool surface over HTTP.

OAuth: installed-app (desktop) flow via `google-auth-oauthlib`'s `InstalledAppFlow.
run_local_server()` — a loopback HTTP listener receives the redirect after browser consent.
This is the only correct flow for a process that is not itself a public web server.

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GOOGLE_DOCS_MCP_CLIENT_ID` | none | OAuth Desktop-app client ID |
| `GOOGLE_DOCS_MCP_CLIENT_SECRET` | none | OAuth client secret |
| `GOOGLE_DOCS_MCP_TOKEN_PATH` | `<repo>/data/token.json` | cached token location |
| `GOOGLE_DOCS_MCP_OAUTH_PORT` | `0` (OS picks) | fixed loopback redirect port |
| `GOOGLE_DOCS_MCP_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | webapp backend bind host |
| `GOOGLE_DOCS_MCP_PORT` | `11972` | webapp backend bind port |
| `GOOGLE_DOCS_MCP_PREFAB_APPS` | `1` | set `0` to skip registering Prefab App tools |
| `LIBREOFFICE_MCP_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:10981/mcp` | libreoffice-mcp endpoint for `google_docs_convert_advanced` |
| `GOOGLE_DOCS_MCP_SYNC_CONFIG_PATH` | `<repo>/data/sync_config.json` | sync config location |
| `GOOGLE_DOCS_MCP_SYNC_MANIFEST_PATH` | `<repo>/data/sync_manifest.json` | sync manifest location |

## Onboarding summary

Requires a Google Cloud project with the Docs API and Drive API enabled, and an OAuth 2.0
Desktop-app client (not Web application). Free for personal use, no billing account required.
Full walkthrough: docs/ONBOARDING.md. Common pitfalls: "unverified app" warning is expected
and safe to bypass for your own client; wrong client type ("Web application" instead of
"Desktop app") causes a redirect_uri_mismatch on `start_oauth`.

## Troubleshooting quick index

- All calls `not_configured` → OAuth client env vars unset → docs/ONBOARDING.md
- All calls `not_authenticated` → run `start_oauth`
- `start_oauth` hangs after browser consent → firewall blocking loopback redirect, or stale tab
- `permission` on a doc you own → wrong signed-in Google account
- `not_found` with a URL-copied id → strip the URL down to just the id segment
- `redirect_uri_mismatch` → OAuth client created as Web application, needs to be Desktop app

## Development

`uv sync --extra dev`, `just test` (pytest, all Google API calls mocked via
`unittest.mock.MagicMock` standing in for `googleapiclient.discovery.Resource` — no real
credentials needed to run the test suite), `just lint` (ruff check + format --check), `just ci`
(both). Declared test doubles documented in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md.
